title: Assumed Atomic Struct Copying
pattern: Writing or reading a non-primitive struct concurrently under the assumption that the assignment operation is atomic.
why_bad: Plain assignments of structures exceeding the CPU's native word size (typically 64 bits) are compiled into multiple separate instructions. Concurrent threads can read half-written structs, resulting in torn reads and corrupt state.
detection: Plain read/write assignments of multi-field structures or types larger than 64-bits across concurrent threads without locking or atomic wrappers.
counterexample: The struct is wrapped in `std::atomic` (only if the platform supports Lock-Free atomic ops of that size) or guarded by a Mutex.
source: Steve McConnell Ch 13, Richard Sites Ch 27
